svg.title: WHO HOLDS THE DEPOT POWER PROBLEM IN NYC?
svg.desc: A bus depot lot in New York City connected to seven organisations. The city’s pupil transportation office builds routes, which sets how many buses a lot must charge. Bus companies, 48 vendors on 99 contracts running to June 2028, run the lots. Con Edison decides capacity and timing and covers up to 90% of utility-side make-ready costs. NYCSBUS’s Zerega depot runs 14 chargers, 268 kW, on an 80 kW limit using software. NYC Buildings rules and FDNY permits apply to any battery from 1 kWh. NYSERDA vouchers help pay for buses and chargers. The school district uses the service but controls no depot.
